- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then gradually decline — suggesting a lag in recognizing downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes, model fails to correct downward quickly; overestimates remain inflated for several days.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price reversion to mean.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when recent history is volatile or downward trending.
- Model reacts too slowly to early signs of price correction; underestimates downward pressure in the first 5–7 days.
- When true price drops sharply, model fails to adjust forecast downward — often underestimates the depth of correction.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in incorporating recent volatility.
- Model does not adequately account for seasonal or cyclical patterns in price behavior (e.g., post-summer dip, pre-holiday spikes).
